recall.minute: Regularisation constrains model complexity so a network generalises instead of memorising; it reduces variance at the cost of slightly more bias. Explicit methods add penalties, L2 (weight decay, shrinks weights) or L1 (drives weights to zero), or change the structure, as dropout does by randomly removing units with probability p during training and scaling so expectations match at test time. Implicit methods include early stopping with patience and restoring the best checkpoint, normalisation, and data augmentation such as flips, crops, Mixup and CutMix. Deep networks also need proper initialisation, Xavier with variance 2/(n_in + n_out) for tanh and He with 2/n_in for ReLU, to avoid vanishing or exploding signals. Batch norm normalises each feature over the mini-batch, learns γ and β and uses running statistics at inference; layer norm normalises over each sample's features and suits RNNs and Transformers. Choose techniques by data size, architecture and compute, tune the learning rate first and the regularisation strength second, and monitor the train–validation gap.
